briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-008
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- water tower top: (24, 104), roof
- solar canopy: (-8, -126), roof
- storage hall: (-115, 19), indoor
- pump house: (106, -143), indoor
- workcell West: (75, -72), indoor
- fuel depot: (-5, -35), outdoor
- parking lot: (-34, 40), outdoor
- water tank: (66, 136), outdoor

Robots:
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3060 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 16 kg), camera, thermal camera. Endurance: 4920 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2640 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Replace the filter cartridge at storage hall. Location: storage hall. Duration: 270 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T6 is finished.
- T2: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T3: Deliver the pressure gauge (12 kg) to workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 12 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 540 s.
- T4: Tighten the valve at fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T8 is finished.
- T5: Photograph fuel depot for the condition report. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T6: Deliver the toolkit (7 kg) to storage hall. Location: storage hall. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg).
- T7: Deliver the sensor box (11 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 11 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T8: Deliver the cable reel (2 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 2 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 120 s.
- T9: Run a thermal scan of solar canopy. Location: solar canopy. Duration: 240 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T10: Run a thermal scan of water tower top. Location: water tower top. Duration: 180 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 360 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1200 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: water tower top (24, 104, a rooftop); solar canopy (-8, -126, a rooftop); storage hall (-115, 19, indoors); pump house (106, -143, indoors); workcell West (75, -72, indoors); fuel depot (-5, -35, outside); parking lot (-34, 40, outside); water tank (66, 136, outside).

The fleet: A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 51 minutes including getting back. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 16 kg at 2 m/s and runs for 82 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera and a thermal camera. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 44 minutes including getting back. D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 8.5 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 19 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Swap the filter cartridge at storage hall - that takes 4.5 minutes on site but only once the toolkit (T6) has arrived.
(T2) Get eyes on water tower top and check the panels - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T3) Workcell West needs the pressure gauge, which weighs 12 kg - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 9 minutes.
(T4) Someone has to tighten the valve at fuel depot - that takes 2.5 minutes on site but only once the cable reel (T8) has arrived.
(T5) Document fuel depot with pictures - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T6) Storage hall needs the toolkit, which weighs 7 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T7) Fuel depot needs the sensor box, which weighs 11 kg - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T8) Get the cable reel (2 kg) over to fuel depot - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 2 minutes.
(T9) Look for overheating equipment around solar canopy - that takes 4 minutes on site.
(T10) Check water tower top for hot spots - that takes 3 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 6 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 20 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
